newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northeast seen in cold snap early next week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northeast seen in cold snap early next week.

text.p: With the official start of spring only a week away, meteorologists expect the northeastern United States to be hit with a cold snap early next week before more seasonal temperatures set in.

"Readings from Sunday to Tuesday will average seven to 11 degrees below normal," said Jon Davis, meteorologist with Smith Barney in Chicago, adding a warming trend will take hold across the Northeastern region by Wednesday.
The U.S. Northeast is the largest heating oil market in the world. Davis expects the region's temperatures to be normal to above normal Friday and Saturday.

Fred Gesser, meteorologist with independent forecaster Weather Express Inc in Omaha, Nebraska, said the much below average temperatures will be concentrated in northern and western New England. For example, he expects temperatures to reach a low of 13 degrees Fahrenheit in Albany Sunday and Monday.
Gesser said temperatures will be warmer in the coastal regions, with Boston experiencing a low of 25 degrees Fahrenheit Sunday and Monday.
The whole region should moderate to normal to above normal temperatures by next Thursday, just in time for the official start of spring, Gesser said.
Forecasters said disparate temperatures are typical during the tailend of winter.

"The middle of March tends to be the peak of the weather transition. In other words, this is the height of the variablity of the jet stream as it switches from a winter to a more spring-like flow," said Smith Barney's Davis.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1620
